description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Trunk is RED on this right now.

The requirement ancora.gate.change_findings says: "A changed file under lib_paths that lies in no subject footprint shall produce change/uncovered_file." The code does not do that. ChangeAnalysis.uncovered_findings/2 (lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex:24) filters on PolicyFiles.classify(path) == :lib, and classify hardcodes priv/, lib/, skills/, and mix.exs (lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:44-56). It never consults lib_paths. This is a code defect against a must, not a spec defect — the requirement text is already correct and must not be edited to match the code.

Two consequences, both live:
1. A project configured with lib_paths: ["src"] silently gets ZERO uncovered-file findings, so the check is inert for any repo that does not use the hardcoded layout.
2. Ancora own trunk is red because of it. main reports 31 change/uncovered_file warnings on vendored priv/spec_review_assets/*.js, priv/spec_init/*.eex, and mix.exs — files no subject tagged test should ever reach. These were previously papered over by Spec-Ack trailers that the squash merge destroyed (see ancora-sfu).

Fix: thread the already-resolved lib_paths into the check. preflight.project is a %Ancora.ProjectInfo{} carrying lib_paths, and preflight is already in scope at the ChangeAnalysis.findings call site (lib/ancora/gate.ex:172). Pass lib_paths through and filter on "path is under one of lib_paths" instead of classify == :lib. For this repo lib_paths resolves to ["lib"], so the 31 findings disappear and the trunk goes green without any acknowledgment.

Do NOT weaken the requirement, do not add a config demotion, and do not add a Spec-Ack trailer. The point is to make the code match a contract that is already right.

Verification: a test proving a file under a CONFIGURED lib_paths (for example lib_paths: ["src"] with src/thing.ex) produces the finding, and a test proving a changed file outside lib_paths (priv/ asset) does not. Both tagged to ancora.gate.change_findings. Existing scenario ancora.gate.scenario.* for uncovered_file must still pass. Full suite green on both CI matrix legs; mix spec.check --base origin/main ends result=pass.

Status note (2026-09-03): IMPLEMENTED and awaiting cold verification. The 'Trunk is RED right now' framing above is stale; main CI has been green since the 13:17 workflow_dispatch run once the default branch moved to main. The fix is still required for the lib_paths: ["src"] case and to make the code match the must.

- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) lib_paths: ["src"] with a changed src/thing.ex produces change/uncovered_file; (2) a changed priv/ asset or mix.exs outside lib_paths produces nothing; (3) the requirement text is unchanged; (4) no trailer, no config demotion

Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d

Mechanical-remedy bounce count this ticket (if any): 0/2

Auditor scope: read-only, no execution. Every mechanical claim below was re-derived from the repository at /Users/mz/src/ancora-p47-libpaths, not inherited from the VERIFY comment.

MECHANICAL CLAIMS — all six confirmed, none corrected.
- Exactly four files across the stack. Per commit: 5d9cb40..53036d7 touches lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, test/ancora/gate_test.exs; 53036d7..35372ed touches test/support/ancora_case.exs and nothing else. Both inside their own ticket's Allowed touches.
- lib/ancora/policy_files.ex is byte-identical: blob c3b7a5a8e855693c150ac02305ac35f573beb8cc at both 5d9cb40 and HEAD.
- ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 keeps its arity and its @spec; the @spec line does not appear in the diff at all.
- git diff 5d9cb40..HEAD -- .spec/ is empty. The requirement ancora.gate.change_findings at .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md:108 still reads "A changed file under lib_paths that lies in no subject's footprint shall produce change/uncovered_file", priority must.
- No Spec-Ack trailer. Both commit bodies are a single subject line; git log --format=%(trailers) is empty for both.
- .spec/config.yml identical: blob c7faf42773c1589e701a22e123ded6047b2c9751 at both ends.

1. THE :__lib_paths__ SENTINEL — inelegant, not a correctness hazard. Note.
There are exactly two callers of findings/5. Production is lib/ancora/gate.ex:176, and it supplies the key unconditionally three lines above at :158, inside the same pipeline expression that builds the map. No branch, no alternate construction, no path where the map is assembled without the key. The only key-less caller is a test, test/ancora/gate_test.exs:148, which passes %{} and relies on the ["lib"] default. So the default is unreachable from production, exactly as the verifier said.

Three things make it safer than the verifier argued, all checked here:
- SubjectFiles.build/2 returns %{String.t() => MapSet.t()}. The sentinel is an atom. A subject id can never collide with it.
- The footprints local in gate.ex is read in exactly one place, the findings/5 call at :176. The polluted map never reaches another consumer.
- Map.pop runs at change_analysis.ex:21, before the Map.values |> reduce(&MapSet.union/2) at :22, so the list value never reaches MapSet.union.
A nil lib_paths would defeat the default (Map.pop returns nil for a present-but-nil key, and Enum.any?(nil, _) raises) but it cannot occur: ProjectInfo has @enforce_keys [:root, :app, :lib_paths] and validate_lib_paths/1 rejects anything that is not a non-empty list of non-empty binaries, failing construction with {:env, ...}.
Design preference only. The ticket asked for the public arity to stay put.

2. THE BOUNDARY HELPER — a real divergence, and the verifier's claim here is too strong. Note, escalated rather than bounced.
under_lib_path?/2 (change_analysis.ex:30) does String.trim_trailing(lib_path, "/") before matching. source_path?/2 (derive/module_locator.ex:155) does not; it matches on lib_path <> "/" raw. I checked for normalization upstream and there is none: String.trim_trailing occurs exactly once in all of lib/, in the new helper, and neither Config.parse_string_list/5 nor ProjectInfo.validate_lib_paths/1 touches trailing slashes.

So with lib_paths: ["src/"] the two disagree on a real path. under_lib_path?("src/thing.ex", ["src/"]) is true, so the file becomes an uncovered_file candidate. source_path?("src/thing.ex", ["src/"]) is false, because it tests the prefix "src//", so ModuleLocator never indexes the file as a source, it can never enter any subject footprint, and the finding can never be cleared by tagging. That is an unclearable false positive rather than the pre-fix silence.

The VERIFY comment states that a trailing-slash config "src/" behaves identically. That experiment used an untagged src file, which is flagged either way, so it could not distinguish the two implementations. The claim is not supported by the evidence given.

Not a bounce, for three reasons. The defect lives in source_path?/2, which predates this ticket and sits in lib/ancora/derive/**, explicitly Out of Scope for ancora-p47, so the implementer could not have fixed it here. Demonstrating the end-to-end false positive needs a gate run with a tagged source under a trailing-slash lib_path, and this audit has no execution, so per the materiality rule it is a Note and an escalation, not a read-based bounce. And the verdict does not change: the normal configs (["lib"], ["src"]) are unaffected.
Recommend a follow-up ticket to make source_path?/2 trim, or better, to give both call sites one shared helper.
The other two differences are fine. source_path?/2 additionally requires a .ex/.exs extension; under_lib_path?/2 correctly omits that, because the requirement says "a changed file under lib_paths", not a changed source file. Its path == lib_path clause is effectively unreachable behind its own extension guard, since it would need a lib_path that is itself an .ex file.

3. THE TWO NEW TESTS — neither passes for the wrong reason.
Both carry @tag spec: "ancora.gate.change_findings", and that id exists in the spec at :108.
"changed source under configured lib_paths is reported" writes .spec/config.yml with lib_paths: ["src"] and asserts src/thing.ex is flagged. It pins the requirement's contract with a non-default configured path, which is precisely what the hardcoded classify could not satisfy, since classify (policy_files.ex:46) matches only priv/plts/, priv/, test prefixes, governance, doc prefixes, lib prefixes and lib root files, returning :unknown for src/. This is the strong test.
"changed files outside lib_paths are not reported" is a refute pair. The priv/assets/app.js half genuinely reproduces the defect, because classify hits String.starts_with?(path, "priv/") -> :lib at :49. The library.ex half does not fail pre-fix, as the verifier disclosed without being asked; it guards the prefix <> "/" separator against a naive starts_with?(path, "lib"). That is a legitimate regression guard for a real property of the new code, not a test passing for the wrong reason. A refute-only test is weak in isolation, but the positive direction is held by the first new test and by the pre-existing scenario assertion at gate_test.exs:86.

4. s1o SAFETY — the on_exit claim verified from source on this machine, on the versions that matter.
Path read: /Users/mz/.asdf/installs/elixir/1.18.4-otp-26/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/runner.ex. At :371, {ok_or_error, exec_on_exit(test_module, module_pid, timeout)} sits after the receive block closes at :368, outside all three of its branches: the {:ok, context} branch at :357 that runs the module's tests through callback.(context), the setup_all {:error, ...} branch at :362, and the {:DOWN, ...} crash branch at :366. All three converge on :370-371. So the setup_all on_exit fires on every exit path and cannot leak the build directory. Individual test failures cannot skip it either, since run_tests/4 at :382 is an Enum.reduce_while whose only halt is :max_failures_reached, which still returns the accumulator normally.
Confirmed on the second matrix leg too: /Users/mz/.asdf/installs/elixir/1.19.5-otp-28/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/runner.ex:387 has the identical structure. Non-overlap also holds: spawn_test/3 calls receive_test_reply/4 and blocks before exec_on_exit, so two tests of one module cannot run at once.
Citation nit for the record: the VERIFY comment attributes these lines to ExUnit 1.18.1. No 1.18.1 is installed here, and the line numbers quoted (371, 382, 487) match 1.18.4-otp-26 exactly, which is a real CI matrix leg. Substance right, version label off.

5. SCOPE AGAINST INTENT — clean.
No timeout token appears anywhere in git diff 5d9cb40..HEAD; the ExUnit timeout is untouched globally, per test and per module. No added or removed line mentions async or moduletag; the async: true line in ancora_case.exs is diff context, unchanged. Zero removed assert, refute, test or property lines in the test diff. s1o's commit touches only test/support/ancora_case.exs, so lib/**, .github/workflows/ci.yml, mix.exs, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md are all untouched.
The isolation property survives rather than being reverted. It is now per module instead of per call, but each module gets its own path via TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 in setup_all, concurrently running modules therefore never share a directory, and two tests of one module never overlap in time (point 4). Reuse within a module is safe because no call site passes a cd: option (checked: cd: appears nowhere in test/ outside ancora_case.exs), so every subprocess runs mix from the ancora project root and the shared path only ever receives ancora's own artifacts.

6. MINOR NOTES, none blocking.
- The Process dictionary handoff (Process.put in setup, Process.get in run_mix_subprocess) breaks if the helper is ever called from a spawned process or from setup_all, where Process.get returns nil and File.dir?(nil) raises FunctionClauseError. All 30 current call sites are in test bodies. It fails loudly, not silently.
- The VERIFY comment says classify/1 now feeds only Ancora.Next advice "at lib/ancora/next.ex:39". That line actually calls PolicyFiles.policy_target?/1, which reaches classify/1 one hop down through co_change_rule/1 at policy_files.ex:70. The conclusion is right, the cited function is not, and classify/1 is not dead.
- gate_test.exs:148 is named "change analysis is wired to the production change set" but calls findings/5 directly with a hand-built %{}, so it does not exercise the Gate wiring its name promises. Pre-existing, untouched by this ticket.

VERDICT: APPROVE. The verifier was not credulous. It ran its own overlay experiment against pre-fix code rather than accepting the implementer's claim, and it volunteered the weakest piece of its own evidence (the library.ex half). Its single overreach is the trailing-slash "behaves identically" line in point 2, which concerns a pre-existing bug in a file this ticket was forbidden to touch and does not change the verdict. No Gap for the implementer, nothing to send back to the verifier.
Escalating to the orchestrator: the source_path?/2 trailing-slash divergence wants its own ticket, and it wants a both-ways gate run this audit could not perform.

The merged diff carries this ticket's content, lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex and lib/ancora/gate.ex plus 42 lines of new tests in test/ancora/gate_test.exs.
